items.followUp: What information should be identified before drawing a flowchart?

rubric.why: The flowchart requirements include identifying the data entering the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that inputs must be identified.

rubric.why: The flowchart must show what result the problem should produce.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that outputs must be identified.

rubric.why: The operations needed to transform inputs into outputs must be determined.
rubric.description: Determine the processing steps and their order.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the required processing or ordered steps.

rubric.why: Conditions and repeated steps affect the flowchart's structure.
rubric.description: Identify decisions or repetitions and check the flow.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning decisions, repetition, or checking that all paths are covered.

modelAnswer: Analyze the problem and identify its inputs and required outputs.
Determine the processing steps and arrange them in the correct order.
Identify any decisions or steps that must be repeated.
Use the appropriate flowchart symbols to represent the steps and check that every path leads to a valid result.

items.followUp: What is meant by an algorithm in problem solving?

rubric.why: The answer should identify problem solving as the activity being defined.
rubric.description: State that problem solving is the process of addressing a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a process for solving a problem.

rubric.why: Problem solving involves finding a solution, commonly through steps.
rubric.description: Mention finding a solution or following steps to reach one.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it involves finding a solution or reaching it through steps.

modelAnswer: Problem solving is the process of finding a solution to a problem.
It involves understanding the problem and carrying out steps to reach the solution.

items.followUp: Name two more symbols used in a flowchart.

rubric.why: A terminator is one standard flowchart symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct symbol name.

rubric.why: Any other standard flowchart symbol earns the second mark.
rubric.description: Name a second valid flowchart symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct symbol name.

items.followUp: What is a candidate solution to a problem?

rubric.why: A candidate solution is a possible or proposed answer to the problem.
rubric.description: Explain that it is a possible or proposed solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a possible/proposed solution.

rubric.why: A proposed solution must be checked to see whether it meets the problem's requirements.
rubric.description: State that the proposed solution is checked or evaluated against the requirements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning testing, checking, or evaluating it.

modelAnswer: A candidate solution is a possible solution proposed for a problem.
It is checked to see whether it meets the problem's requirements.

items.followUp: Describe the heuristic called “draw a picture.”

rubric.why: Act it out is a problem-solving technique that represents the problem through actions or a simulation.
rubric.description: State that the problem is acted out or simulated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing acting out or simulating the problem.

rubric.why: Acting out helps reveal the steps or outcome and makes the problem easier to solve.
rubric.description: Explain that the action helps understand or solve the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating its purpose.

modelAnswer: “Act it out” is a problem-solving technique in which the situation is acted out or simulated.
This can help reveal the steps and make the problem easier to understand and solve.

rubric.why: HTML is the abbreviation for HyperText Markup Language.
rubric.description: Give the correct full form of HTML.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct expansion.

modelAnswer: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.

items.followUp: What text will appear on the webpage, and how will it be formatted?

rubric.why: The h1 element contains the text that is displayed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing “My First Heading”.

rubric.why: The h1 tag formats the text as a top-level heading.
rubric.description: State that it appears as a large, top-level heading.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as an h1 or large heading.

modelAnswer: It is displayed as a large, top-level heading.

rubric.why: Dividing 59 by 16 gives quotient 3 and remainder 11.
rubric.description: Show the quotient and remainder from division by 16.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct division step or quotient and remainder.

rubric.why: The hexadecimal digit for decimal 11 is B, so the result is 3B.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer, 3B.
